skill.name: storage-debug-instrumentation
skill.description: Add debugging and observability tools for PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and application startup, including drift detection, inspection endpoints, and a Next.js dashboard.
skill.summary: Instrument storage systems and application startup for focused diagnosis through metrics, drift checks, APIs, and a dashboard.
skill.author: BenderFendor

security_audit.summary: All 55 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, localhost examples, and fixed verification instructions. However, the workflow creates debug routes that expose raw storage content and operational metadata without required access controls or redaction. Add production safeguards before publishing or deploying these routes.

remediation.issue: Debug endpoints lack required access controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require authenticated administrator access, disable routes outside approved environments, and reject requests when secure configuration is absent.

remediation.issue: Raw storage records and operational metadata may contain sensitive information.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive fields, return bounded samples, enforce pagination limits, log access, and test that unauthorized users receive no diagnostic data.

content.user_title: Diagnose Storage Drift and Startup Performance
content.value_statement: Storage failures and slow startup phases are difficult to trace across PostgreSQL and ChromaDB. This skill guides metrics, inspection endpoints, drift checks, and dashboard implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a thread-safe startup metrics service for phase timings and annotations.
Instruments vector store initialization and FastAPI startup phases with durations and operational metadata.
Adds paginated inspection helpers for PostgreSQL articles and ChromaDB documents.
Compares PostgreSQL mappings with ChromaDB identifiers to identify missing and dangling entries.
Defines typed frontend fetchers and a multi-tab Next.js diagnostic dashboard.
limitations: Provides an implementation workflow, not ready-to-run source files.
Assumes a Python FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and a Next.js frontend with matching project paths.
Does not define authentication, authorization, redaction, or environment restrictions for debug routes.
Specifies linting and manual verification but does not require automated security or integration tests.

use_cases.title: Trace Slow Application Startup
use_cases.description: Measure backend startup phases and identify expensive database, cache, scheduler, migration, or vector store operations.

use_cases.title: Find Storage Synchronization Drift
use_cases.description: Compare PostgreSQL article mappings with ChromaDB identifiers to locate missing vectors and dangling entries.

use_cases.title: Build an Operations Dashboard
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js interface for startup metrics, storage browsing, filters, pagination, and drift summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Map the Existing Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository and map the files named by the storage debug skill. Identify missing paths, framework differences, and required adaptations before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Instrument Application Startup
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement startup metrics for this backend. Time each existing startup phase, preserve error behavior, avoid sensitive metadata, and add focused tests.

prompt_templates.title: Add Storage Drift Diagnostics
prompt_templates.prompt: Add paginated PostgreSQL and ChromaDB inspection helpers plus a drift report. Use bounded queries, redact sensitive fields, and test missing and dangling records.

prompt_templates.title: Deliver the Secure Debug Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the complete storage debug workflow in this repository. Preserve project patterns, secure every route, redact sensitive fields, add tests, and report verification.

output_examples.input: Diagnose which startup phase is slow.
output_examples.output: Database initialization is the slowest phase at 4.2 seconds. Cache preload follows at 1.1 seconds. Review database connection and query timing.
PostgreSQL contains 1,204 mapped articles. ChromaDB contains 1,198 entries. Six records are missing from ChromaDB, and no dangling vectors were found.
The dashboard contains Startup, ChromaDB, PostgreSQL, and Drift tabs. Each data view supports loading, errors, refresh, filtering, and pagination.

best_practices: Restrict every debug route to authenticated administrators and approved environments.
Redact sensitive fields and expose bounded samples instead of complete records or collections.
Keep instrumentation nonblocking, preserve original failures, and test pagination, drift logic, authorization, and error states.
anti_patterns: Do not expose debug endpoints or dashboards on a public network without strong access controls.
Do not return entire storage collections, secrets, credentials, personal data, or unrestricted operational metadata.
Do not let instrumentation block startup, suppress exceptions, or change production storage behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill add?
faq.answer: It guides additive startup instrumentation, storage helpers, debug endpoints, frontend API bindings, and a Next.js dashboard.

faq.question: Does it change the database schema?
faq.answer: No. The workflow states that changes are additive and require no schema changes.

faq.question: Which storage systems are supported?
faq.answer: The documented workflow targets PostgreSQL for relational articles and ChromaDB for vector documents.

faq.question: Can the debug routes run in production?
faq.answer: Only after adding authentication, authorization, redaction, bounded responses, audit logging, and environment controls.

faq.question: Does the skill include ready-to-run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides a detailed implementation and verification checklist for an agent to apply to a compatible repository.

faq.question: How should the implementation be verified?
faq.answer: Run the fixed Ruff check, test local endpoints, and confirm dashboard refresh, filters, pagination, drift results, and startup durations.
